messages:
Olga: Quick follow-up from today's runtime all-hands. PMs want three bullets for the public roadmap: 1) short canary window for kernel-v5, 2) which telemetry fields will be shown to Product, 3) a one-line explanation of automatic fallback we can reuse.

Ravi: Canary window: 2026-01-12 -> 2026-01-19 for a focused canary pool; broader rollout depends on health signals.

Marta: Telemetry plan: per-kernel p50/p90/p95/p99 histograms, seq-length buckets (256/512/1024/2048+), kv-cache hit/miss, per-node memory deltas, and an estimated cost-per-token metric. Product gets aggregated + opt-in per-tenant views.

Chris: Recommended blurb: "Kernel rollouts are staged with canaries and automatic fallback to healthy variants; customers can pin kernels or opt-out via Console or SDK flags." Feel free to use that.

Jun: Perf note: v5 improves throughput but increases transient KV on long sequences. For interactive workloads recommend microbatch=8-16; for high throughput use batch>=64. Add a note about quantized variants shifting the sweet spot.

deploy-bot: [notice] 2026-01-13T03:04 - Canary pool alert: transient memory variance on 80G nodes; 7% traffic diverted to fallback variants.

Ravi: Short-term mitigations: drop canary default batch_size to 16, divert heavy sessions to last-stable variant, and enable KV prefetch throttle. We'll script toggles for quick rollback.

Marta: Patch plan: reduce KV prealloc slab and short-circuit empty writes; patch ETA ~30-48h. Telemetry endpoints will be published in the Console docs and linked here.

Olga: Action items recap: Marta = publish telemetry endpoints + ETA; Ravi = ops toggle scripts and playbook; Chris = one-line blurb to include in roadmap. PMs want a 1-pager mapping kernel->latency/cost/batch recommendations. Can we have drafts in 48h?

Jun: I'll produce a perf appendix with sample bench commands and a small table of median/tail numbers for 512/1024 seq.

Olga: Thanks all 44d please drop links here when ready.
